drafted_from: tool:resync-an-elestio-pipeline's own row (its words, input schema and invoke) and do-work/resync-an-elestio-pipeline.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "I pushed e545104 to the school site's branch; resync its Elestio pipeline 26310 and tell me when it serves that commit." It asks Elestio to redeploy the pipeline and answers ok, the commit before and after, and the seconds it took.
no_lists_because: It keeps no row: it redeploys one pipeline and returns what Elestio says; the caller records the outcome where its job keeps them.
instructions: 1. Hold an Elestio API token in the vault as elestio-api-key, bound only to api.elest.io (Elestio dashboard, Account, Security, Create token, for the pipeline's project).
2. Push the change to the branch the pipeline builds; a push alone does not redeploy it.
3. Call this tool with the account email, the project id, the CI/CD target's vmID, the pipeline id and the pushed commit.

4. Read ok: true means the Resync run the call made (a new row in the pipeline's history) ended Success on that commit; otherwise reason says what it saw (the run failed or was canceled, deployed another commit, or did not end within wait_seconds).
5. A call waits at most 100 s. When it answers still_running, call it again with run_id set to the run it named: it follows that run and asks nothing new, until the run ends.
6. For the site's downtime, probe its address once a second while this runs; this tool reads only Elestio's own record.

worked_examples.title: Redeploy the school site after a push
worked_examples.ask: I pushed e545104 to the school site's branch; resync its pipeline and confirm it serves it.
worked_examples.given: A pipeline that builds the branch the commit was pushed to, and elestio-api-key in the vault.
